The building to be used for the Alma Neighborhood Center is located adjacent to West Alma Avenue. Since the Ldn 60 to 70 dBA noise zone extends 100 feet south of Alma, the building probably is within the high noise zone and should be considered for noise reducing remedial measures.
For noise generated by auto traffic, sound barriers are sometimes used as a means of mitigation. Such barriers can give up to 15 dB attenuation, but their effectiveness is very dependent on the local geometry and often height of walls necessary are unsatisfactory for aesthetic reasons.
The second class of noise impact are associated with construction and demolition activities which are included to some degree in all the projects of all programs. Construction noise varies, depending on the equipment being used. Appendix F gives the range of noise levels for various construction equipment. Although construction noise levels are high, they are attenuated by distance, thus, the levels indicated in the table would be reduced by 6 dB, 100 feet from the site, 12 dB when 200 feet and 18 dB, 400 feet distant. Also, intervening buildings will add another 10 to 15 dB attenuation. Thus, at 400 feet, a net attenuation of 33 dB can be expected for many situations, and a 95 dB source noise level would be reduced to 62 dB which is near the acceptable noise level of 60 dB for outdoor areas inducted by EPA (1974); but will be above the residual daytime noise levels of about 50 dBA.
The average noise levels generated during erection and finishing work on domestic housing is 65 to 72 dBA (EPA, 1971). Thus, at 200 feet from the site, exterior noise levels would be attenuated to about 50 dBA, the residual daytime level most of the time. Rehabilitation work would most likely extend over a period of about two or three weeks for most units, and noisy activities would be restricted to about 25% of the total day during daylight hours. If neighboring units are undergoing simultaneous rehabilitation, localized noise levels will be somewhat higher.
Public works projects, rebuilding of streets, curbs, sidewalks and storm and sanitary sewage lines will involve temporary construction related noise impacts. According to EPA (1971), these operations will generate average noise levels of 84 to 88 dBA at 50 feet from the noisiest equipment. Residences facing the street will be subjected to this level during the periods of noisiest operations. The row of homes behind those adjacent to the street being rebuilt will have the construction noise attenuated by approximately 15 to 20 dBA. Thus, exterior levels of 68 to 73 dBA would be expected in these areas. The time duration of street work at any specific location is not expected to exceed a week or two. Also, activity would be restricted to daylight hours.
